html:
Tommy Douglas was premier of Saskatchewan from 1944 to 1961, leading the first socialist government in North America, and the father of public health care in Canada. Born in Scotland, he was a Baptist minister before entering politics.

His Co-operative Commonwealth Federation government brought in public hospital insurance in 1947. Its medical care plan of 1962, which paid for doctors' visits, set off a strike by Saskatchewan's doctors, but it held.

The federal government of Canada followed with a national medicare law in 1966, and by 1972 every province had joined. Douglas led the New Democratic Party in Parliament from 1961. In 2004 viewers of the CBC voted him the Greatest Canadian. Public health care is now a core part of Canadian identity, as is the Charter, and a contrast with the United States.
